messages.text: Joshua's driver in fatal car crash has trial adjourned

metadata.summary: The trial of Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode, the driver involved in the crash that injured boxer Anthony Joshua and killed two members of his team, has been adjourned until November 17.
metadata.content: Anthony Joshua car crash: Trial of driver involved in fatal collision has hearing adjourned until November 17 | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Anthony Joshua car crash: Trial of driver involved in fatal collision has hearing adjourned until November 17 Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode was driving an SUV that struck a stationary truck on December 29 2025, injuring Anthony Joshua and killing two members of his team; He is facing a four-count charge Thursday 10 September 2026 18:47, UK Image: Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode (right) pictured arriving at court in January The trial of Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode, the driver involved in the crash that injured boxer Anthony Joshua and killed two members of his team, has been adjourned until November 17. The case, which began in January at a magistrate court in Ogun State, was adjourned from September 10 as proceedings continued over charges arising from the fatal crash on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. Joshua's personal trainer, Latif Ayodele, and strength and conditioning coach, Sina Ghami, were killed. Kayode faces charges including dangerous driving causing death, reckless and negligent driving, driving without due care and attention, and operating a vehicle without a valid national driver's licence. The 46-year-old Kayode denies the charges. Prosecutors allege that Kayode was attempting to overtake another vehicle when the SUV carrying Joshua and his team crashed into a stationary truck. messages.text: Overton, Leach help Somerset remain top with crushing win at Leicestershire

metadata.summary: Craig Overton and Jack Leach combined to inflict a 377-run thrashing on Leicestershire and keep Somerset top of the Rothesay County Championship with only two more rounds to go.
metadata.content: County Championship cricket: Craig Overton, Jack Leach help Somerset remain top with crushing win at Leicestershire | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content County Championship cricket: Craig Overton, Jack Leach help Somerset remain top with crushing win at Leicestershire After title rivals Warwickshire claimed victory inside two days against Glamorgan, leaders Somerset responded with aplomb against Leicestershire to clinch 377-run victory and return top of the Rothesay County Championship as Craig Overton and Jack Leach stood out Thursday 10 September 2026 19:02, UK Image: Craig Overton Craig Overton and Jack Leach combined to inflict a 377-run thrashing on Leicestershire and keep Somerset top of the Rothesay County Championship with only two more rounds to go. After title rivals Warwickshire claimed victory inside two days against Glamorgan, leaders Somerset responded with aplomb. Henry Nicholls' unbeaten 100 helped the visitors declare on 316-5 to set Leicestershire an insurmountable victory target of 523. The real question was whether Somerset could wrap up this latest triumph with a day to spare and Leicestershire only managed to bat out 45.1 overs, with Overton the pick of the bowlers - 4-33 - and England's forgotten man Leach taking 3-30 to dismiss the hosts for 145. Max Verstappen says the new Madring F1 circuit is "probably a car killer" with several drivers expecting a disruptive Spanish Grand Prix weekend. The close proximity of the walls at the high-speed track, which includes a big banked corner in the middle sector, was the big talk of the paddock on Thursday. messages.text: De Zerbi 'was the key' - Fernandes on his Spurs switch and trophy ambitions

metadata.summary: Spurs may have failed to win any of their first three Premier League games this season, but summer signing Matheus Fernandes is convinced he has joined a squad set to start fighting for trophies.
metadata.content: Matheus Fernandes interview: Spurs midfielder on the passion of head coach Roberto De Zerbi and trophy ambitions | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Matheus Fernandes interview: Spurs midfielder on the passion of head coach Roberto De Zerbi and trophy ambitions Tottenham searching for first goal and first win of the Premier League season but £85m Matheus Fernandes says the squad with "a lot of quality" is aiming to fight for trophies; watch Tottenham vs Everton live on Sky from 5pm on Saturday; kick-off 5.30pm By Interview: Adam Smith | Words: Peter Smith Thursday 10 September 2026 17:59, UK Image: Matheus Fernandes says Roberto De Zerbi was key to his £85m transfer to Tottenham Spurs may have failed to win any of their first three Premier League games this season, but summer signing Matheus Fernandes is convinced he has joined a squad set to start fighting for trophies. The £85m midfielder was wanted by a list of clubs after impressing for West Ham last season, with Man Utd keen on a deal but ultimately unable to go head-to-head with Spurs on the fee. For Fernandes, it was his conversations with head coach Roberto De Zerbi which persuaded him the north London project was for him. "I spoke with the Mister and he was the key for this decision," Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of the Saturday Night Football clash with Everton.
